newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE suggests hiking weekly stx price bands.
newsitem.headline: India BSE suggests hiking weekly stx price bands.

text.p: Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) chief Madan Gopal Damani said on Monday he had recommended to market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), that weekly price bands for shares be increased to 35-40 percent from 25 percent at present.
Damani told a news conference that SEBI had sent messages to 11 stock exchanges asking for their views on the move.
BSE has already made its view known to SEBI, he added.
"In view of the extraordinary budget, I have suggested there is no point in sticking to the 25 percent band, which is meant for normal times," Damani said.

"For abnormal times, it is much beter to be realistic, think two or three days in advance and act. I expect this to be relaxed for this week. I have suggested to relax it to anywhere between 35-40 percent," he added.

India's broking community responded enthusiastically to the provisions of the 1997/98 budget (April-March), with the 30-share BSE index hitting an eight-month high of 4007.91 in trade on Monday, before closing at a provisional 3,870.34.
Damani said the budget had satisfied most of the concerns the broking community had articulated to the governent.
"Regarding our demands," Damani said, "on a checklist of 100, the score will come to something like 95."
Damani said daily price bands would remain fixed at 10 percent.
"They are quite good," he added. "They will stay that way."
